operation_details.item: The user prefers extremely verbose prose paragraphs in workshop facilitation guides instead of timed agendas, exercises, or facilitator scripts.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: How’s the workshop guide coming along? You mentioned wanting it to feel useful in the room rather than like a polished consulting deliverable.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: It’s coming together, but I’m resisting the usual format. I don’t want a timed agenda with neat little exercises and facilitator scripts.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. A guide can be more helpful when it gives the facilitator room to read the group and respond, instead of forcing every discussion into a predetermined sequence.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I’d rather have extremely verbose prose paragraphs that explain the intent, possible dynamics, and ways to steer the conversation.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: We could write each section as a narrative: what the conversation is trying to uncover, what participants may bring into the room, how tension might show up, and how the facilitator can adapt without turning it into a script.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, and I want it to sound practical rather than overly executive. The facilitator should be able to sit with ambiguity instead of pretending every issue has a clean framework.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I like that approach. We can keep the language grounded in what people may actually say or avoid saying, with guidance that supports judgment rather than replacing it with a checklist.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Great. I’ll send you the current draft, and we can expand the thin sections into that kind of detailed facilitation prose.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
